meta.title: Scope — where a task's `scope` field comes from
meta.frame: The task-create skill's '## Scope' section, as a graph instead of prose. Answers: where does scope come from, in what order, what does NOT influence it, what goes wrong, and what to do about it. Not an implementation trace of taskfw/scope.py -- see for_create's docstring for the actual code path (task:ff8e0dfa).

relation_types.determines: the left node decides the right node's value when every higher-precedence node is absent
relation_types.does_not_affect: a plausible-looking influence that turns out to do nothing here
relation_types.causes: left node's behavior produces right node as a consequence
relation_types.fixes: left node is the corrective action for the right node's problem
relation_types.reports: left node is returned alongside right node so its source is visible

nodes.label: tasks__create(repo=...)
nodes.definition: A repo path or a scope value the caller names. Wins over everything else. scope_source = explicit.

nodes.label: Absolute `files` that all sit in one git checkout
nodes.definition: Used only if every absolute path has a .git ancestor and they all resolve to the same git: scope. Relative paths are ignored. Files spanning two repos, or outside any git checkout, give no answer. scope_source = files.

nodes.label: Directory the taskfw MCP server was launched in
nodes.definition: The fallback, used only when neither of the above applies. Fixed once, at session start, so it is wherever the session began, not where the work is. scope_source = server_cwd.

nodes.label: Agent running `cd` in a shell tool
Harness's reported "current working directory"
nodes.definition: Can change mid-conversation (e.g. after a shell cd). Looks like it should matter. Doesn't.

nodes.label: task.scope (git:<host>/<path> / path:<abs> / hint:<text>)
nodes.definition: Set once at tasks__create, from the highest-precedence source present. Never re-derived afterwards.

nodes.label: scope_source in the tasks__create response
nodes.definition: explicit / files / server_cwd. server_cwd is the one to look at twice.

nodes.label: Session creates a task for a different repo than it started in, with no repo= and no absolute files
Task filed under the wrong project
nodes.definition: Nothing errors. The task just sits under a scope that doesn't match its work, and every scoped read miscounts it.

nodes.label: Pass repo=<abs repo path> to tasks__create
nodes.definition: The fix before the fact: when the session's start directory is not the task's repo.

nodes.label: tasks__update(task_id, scope="git:<host>/<path>")
nodes.definition: The fix after the fact. Use the target repo's actual git remote, not a guessed name.
